title: Mule Account Velocity Pattern
description: Detects rapid inbound transfers from multiple unique senders followed by immediate outbound movement, typical of money mule activity. This rule is a shared component applicable to TP-0001, TP-0002, TP-0011, and TP-0022.
falsepositives: Legitimate payroll processing accounts receiving from multiple employers
Business accounts with normal multi-party receivables

title: Infostealer Credential Dump Velocity
description: Detects rapid credential dump patterns where many unique credentials are harvested from a single host in a short timeframe. Infostealers such as RedLine, Lumma, and Vidar typically exfiltrate dozens to hundreds of stored credentials within seconds of execution, producing a burst of credential-access events from one endpoint.

detection.condition: selection and not filter_legitimate | count(distinct target_credential) by host_id > 20

falsepositives: Legitimate credential manager software performing bulk synchronization
Enterprise password vault agents rotating stored credentials

title: Session Cookie Exfiltration Pattern
description: Detects session token and cookie theft patterns in log data indicative of infostealer activity. Stealers like Lumma and Raccoon target browser cookie stores to extract active session tokens, enabling session hijacking without requiring credentials. This rule monitors for suspicious access to cookie databases and exfiltration of session-bearing data.
falsepositives: Third-party browser extensions with legitimate cookie management functionality
Endpoint backup solutions that include browser profile data

title: Browser Credential Store Access
description: Detects unusual access to browser credential stores (Login Data, logins.json, key3.db/key4.db) by non-browser processes. Infostealers such as RedLine and Vidar systematically read these SQLite databases to extract saved usernames and passwords for banking portals and other financial services.

detection.condition: selection and not filter_browser_processes and not filter_av

falsepositives: Password migration tools used during browser transitions
IT-managed credential audit tools on corporate endpoints

title: Stealer C2 Beacon Pattern
description: Detects command-and-control callback patterns typical of Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) stealers. RedLine, Lumma, and StealC use distinctive C2 communication patterns including HTTP POST requests with base64-encoded payloads to newly registered domains, often on non-standard ports or with characteristic URI patterns.
falsepositives: Legitimate PHP-based applications using similar URI naming conventions
New SaaS platforms with recently registered domains

title: Credential Testing After Dump
description: Detects rapid credential validation attempts occurring shortly after a credential dump event. After infostealers exfiltrate harvested credentials, threat actors typically run automated validation to identify which stolen credentials are still active, producing a burst of login attempts across multiple banking portals from the attacker's infrastructure.
falsepositives: Corporate SSO gateways performing health checks against multiple accounts
Automated monitoring systems testing service account connectivity

title: Infostealer Exfiltration Archive Creation
description: Detects creation of archive files containing credential-related file patterns consistent with infostealer packaging behavior. Stealers like RedLine and Vidar collect credentials, cookies, autofill data, and crypto wallet files into a ZIP or RAR archive before exfiltrating them to the C2 server.
falsepositives: Legitimate backup software creating archives of user profile data
IT support tools collecting diagnostic bundles that include browser data

title: Multiple Account Access from Single Source
description: Detects multiple distinct banking accounts being accessed from a single device or IP address within a short timeframe. This pattern is consistent with an attacker using stolen credentials from an infostealer dump to sequentially access compromised accounts for reconnaissance or initial positioning before fraudulent transactions.

detection.condition: selection | count(distinct account_id) by source_ip > 5 or selection | count(distinct account_id) by device_fingerprint > 3

falsepositives: Shared corporate NAT gateways where multiple employees access accounts from same public IP
Household devices shared among family members with separate accounts

title: Stolen Session Token Replay
description: Detects session token replay from a different geographic location or device than the original authenticating session. When infostealers exfiltrate active session cookies, attackers import them into antidetect browsers to hijack authenticated sessions without triggering login-based detections. This rule correlates session token usage across differing geolocations and device fingerprints.

detection.condition: selection and not filter_same_context | count() by session_token > 1

falsepositives: Users connecting via VPN whose egress IP changes geographic region mid-session
Mobile users roaming internationally with active banking sessions

title: Autofill Data Harvesting
description: Detects form autofill data extraction patterns consistent with infostealer behavior. Stealers like RedLine and Raccoon target browser autofill databases (Web Data, formhistory.sqlite) to harvest stored PII including names, addresses, phone numbers, and payment card details that facilitate downstream fraud.

detection.condition: selection and not filter_browsers and not filter_system

falsepositives: Browser profile migration utilities reading autofill databases during import
Form-filling accessibility tools for users with disabilities

title: Crypto Wallet Seed Phrase Exfiltration
description: Detects wallet seed phrase and private key extraction attempts targeting cryptocurrency wallets. Infostealers such as RedLine, Vidar, and StealC include dedicated modules that search for wallet.dat files, seed phrase backups, and keystore directories for MetaMask, Exodus, Electrum, and other popular wallets to enable cryptocurrency theft.

detection.condition: (selection_wallet_files or selection_metamask or selection_seed_files) and not filter_wallet_apps

falsepositives: Legitimate wallet backup procedures initiated by the user
Crypto portfolio management tools that aggregate across multiple wallets

title: Login Velocity Anomaly
description: Detects abnormal login attempt velocity from a single source IP or subnet, indicative of automated credential stuffing tools. Legitimate users produce low single-digit login attempts per minute; credential stuffing tools generate dozens to hundreds, often targeting the authentication API directly rather than the web login form.

detection.condition: selection and not filter_internal | count() by source_ip > 50

falsepositives: Load testing or penetration testing activities against authentication endpoints
Misconfigured monitoring scripts with aggressive polling intervals

title: Geographic Impossibility Login
description: Detects login attempts from geographically impossible locations within a short timeframe. When a user authenticates from one country and a second authentication occurs from a distant country within a window that makes physical travel impossible, it strongly indicates credential compromise and concurrent use by an attacker.

detection.condition: selection | near by user_id | where geo_distance(src.geo_lat, src.geo_lon, dst.geo_lat, dst.geo_lon) > 1000 and time_diff < 60m

falsepositives: Users employing VPN services that change egress country between sessions
Corporate proxy chains routing through geographically distributed data centers

title: Device Fingerprint Anomaly
description: Detects a known device fingerprint presenting with changed underlying characteristics such as OS version, screen resolution, timezone, or installed fonts. Attackers using antidetect browsers (Multilogin, GoLogin, Dolphin Anty) import stolen device fingerprints but often have mismatches in lower-level hardware attributes that this rule correlates.

detection.condition:
selection | where device_fingerprint in known_device_fingerprints and (
  os_version != baseline.os_version
  or screen_resolution != baseline.screen_resolution
  or timezone_offset != baseline.timezone_offset
  or webgl_renderer != baseline.webgl_renderer
  or canvas_hash != baseline.canvas_hash
)

falsepositives: Users who updated their OS or browser, changing underlying fingerprint attributes
Legitimate device reconfigurations such as connecting external monitors

title: Combo List Iteration Pattern
description: Detects sequential username patterns typical of combo list iteration during credential stuffing attacks. Attackers feed sorted credential lists into stuffing tools, producing login attempts where usernames appear in alphabetical or near-alphabetical order with minimal timing variation between attempts, a pattern never seen in organic user behavior.

detection.condition: selection | count(distinct username) by source_ip > 15 and stddev(inter_event_time) by source_ip < 500ms

falsepositives: Automated batch user provisioning systems that test accounts sequentially
QA test suites running ordered account validation during deployments

title: Distributed Credential Stuffing
description: Detects low-and-slow distributed credential stuffing attacks spread across multiple source IPs to evade per-IP rate limiting. Advanced attackers use residential proxy networks and botnets to distribute attempts, making each source IP appear benign while the aggregate attack targets many accounts. This rule aggregates failed login patterns across source IPs sharing common characteristics.

detection.condition: selection and selection_characteristics | count(distinct source_ip) by user_agent > 20 and count(distinct username) by user_agent > 50 and max(count() by source_ip) < 5

falsepositives: Large-scale legitimate user activity from a popular browser version during peak hours
CDN or reverse-proxy traffic aggregation that normalizes user-agent strings

title: Residential Proxy Login Attempt
description: Detects login attempts originating from known residential proxy networks. Credential stuffing actors increasingly route attacks through residential proxies (Luminati/Bright Data, Oxylabs, SmartProxy) to appear as legitimate home users and bypass IP-reputation blocklists. This rule correlates source IPs against residential proxy threat intelligence feeds.
falsepositives: Legitimate users whose ISP IP ranges overlap with residential proxy exit nodes
Privacy-conscious users routing through VPN services that share residential IP pools

title: Credential Spray Single Password
description: Detects password spraying attacks where a single password (or small set of passwords) is tested across many accounts. Unlike traditional credential stuffing which uses unique username-password pairs, password spraying tries common or recently breached passwords against a large account population to avoid per-account lockout thresholds.

detection.condition: selection | count(distinct username) by password_hash > 20 and count(distinct password_hash) by source_ip < 3

falsepositives: Batch account creation workflows where a default password is assigned to many accounts
Automated test frameworks using a shared test password across test accounts

title: Beneficiary Change Velocity Anomaly
description: Detects multiple beneficiary additions or modifications on a single account within a short time window. Rapid beneficiary changes are a strong pre-cursor to payment diversion fraud, where an attacker positions new destination accounts before initiating unauthorized wires.
falsepositives: Corporate treasury teams onboarding multiple new vendors during month-end
Business accounts setting up payroll beneficiaries for the first time

title: Rapid Contact Information Change
description: Detects when email, phone number, and mailing address are all changed on an account within a short window. A full contact information swap is a hallmark of account takeover where the attacker locks out the legitimate owner before executing fraud.

detection.condition: (selection_email and selection_phone and selection_address) | count() by account_id >= 3

falsepositives: Customer relocating and updating all contact details with their bank simultaneously
Account remediation after a legitimate customer service request

title: MFA Method Switch Before High-Value Transaction
description: Detects when an account's multi-factor authentication method is changed (e.g., from hardware token to SMS or email OTP) shortly before a high-value wire or ACH transaction is initiated. Attackers downgrade MFA to a method they control prior to executing fraud.
falsepositives: Customer who lost their hardware token and is making a legitimate scheduled payment
Planned MFA migration events by IT or security teams

title: Dormant Account Reactivation
description: Detects accounts with no transactional activity for 90 or more days that suddenly initiate financial transactions. Dormant accounts are frequently targeted by attackers because they are less likely to be monitored and credential compromise may go unnoticed.
falsepositives: Seasonal businesses that operate on annual cycles (e.g., tax preparation firms)
Estate or trust accounts activated for legitimate distributions

title: Alert Threshold Modification
description: Detects when a user modifies their own transaction alert thresholds or disables notifications via online banking or mobile app. Attackers raise alert thresholds or suppress notifications to prevent the legitimate account holder from being alerted to unauthorized transactions.
falsepositives: Customers who intentionally adjust alert settings to reduce notification fatigue
Business accounts adjusting thresholds for expected high-value transactions

title: Wire Beneficiary Name Mismatch
description: Detects when the wire beneficiary name provided by the originator does not match the account holder name at the receiving institution. Name mismatches on wire transfers are a strong indicator of payment diversion fraud where funds are redirected to accounts controlled by the attacker.
falsepositives: Payments to businesses using a DBA (doing business as) name different from legal entity name
Wire transfers to joint accounts where one holder's name is provided

title: Power of Attorney or Authorized Signer Change
description: Detects changes to power of attorney designations or authorized signers on commercial and business accounts. Fraudsters may socially engineer or forge POA documents to gain control of business accounts, enabling them to initiate high-value transactions.
falsepositives: Legitimate corporate governance changes such as new CFO or treasurer appointment
Succession planning updates on trust accounts

title: Account Type Conversion Anomaly
description: Detects suspicious account type conversions such as savings-to-checking or personal-to-business. These conversions can unlock higher transaction limits, wire capabilities, or ACH origination, which attackers exploit to move larger amounts after taking over a limited account.
falsepositives: Small business owners legitimately converting a personal account to a business account
Customers upgrading account tiers for better interest rates or features

title: First-Time International Wire to New Country
description: Detects international wire transfers sent to a country that has no prior transaction history for the originating account. First-time international wires, especially to high-risk corridors, are a key indicator of business email compromise and payment diversion schemes.
falsepositives: Companies expanding into new international markets with legitimate vendor payments
Individual customers sending family remittances to a new country for the first time

title: Transaction Amount Clustering Near Reporting Threshold
description: Detects transactions that cluster just below regulatory reporting thresholds ($3,000 for international transfers, $10,000 for CTR filing). Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements is itself a federal offense and a strong indicator of money laundering or fraud monetization.

detection.condition: (selection_under_10k | count() by account_id > 2) or (selection_under_3k | count() by account_id > 2)

falsepositives: Small business owners with legitimately recurring transactions that happen to fall near thresholds
Payroll deposits that naturally cluster at consistent amounts

title: Split Transfer Chain Detection
description: Detects when a large inbound amount is split into multiple smaller outbound transfers to different beneficiaries in sequence. This layering technique is used to obscure the origin and destination of fraudulently obtained funds.

detection.condition: selection_large_inbound | near selection_multiple_outbound by account_id | count(distinct beneficiary_id) by account_id > 2

falsepositives: Businesses receiving large payments and distributing to multiple sub-contractors
Investment accounts rebalancing across multiple fund positions

title: After-Hours Wire Transfer Initiation
description: Detects wire transfers initiated outside the account's established normal business hours. Attackers often execute unauthorized wires during evenings, weekends, or holidays when fraud detection staff and account holders are less likely to notice.

detection.condition: selection and selection_channel and not filter_pre_authorized

falsepositives: International businesses operating across time zones with legitimate after-hours activity
Business owners making urgent payments during personal hours

title: Rapid Outbound Wire After Large Inbound
description: Detects a large outbound wire or ACH transfer initiated within hours of receiving a large inbound deposit. This pass-through pattern is characteristic of compromised accounts being used as intermediary conduits in fraud or money laundering schemes.
falsepositives: Real estate escrow closings with same-day receipt and disbursement
Business accounts receiving client payments and immediately paying suppliers

title: Beneficiary Country Mismatch with Business Profile
description: Detects wire transfers to countries where the account holder has no established business relationship or prior transaction history. Combined with other indicators, this can reveal business email compromise where payment instructions are altered to redirect funds to attacker-controlled accounts in foreign jurisdictions.
falsepositives: Companies sourcing from a new international supplier for the first time
One-time international consulting or service payments

title: Round-Dollar Wire Amount Pattern
description: Detects unusual patterns of wire transfers in round dollar amounts (e.g., $5,000, $10,000, $25,000). While individual round-amount wires are common, a pattern of multiple round-amount wires is atypical for legitimate business payments and may indicate structured or test transactions by fraudsters.
falsepositives: Loan disbursements or payments that are inherently round amounts
Recurring fixed-amount business payments (rent, retainers)

title: ACH Return Rate Anomaly
description: Detects ACH originators with an elevated return or reversal rate exceeding normal thresholds. High ACH return rates (especially R10 unauthorized, R29 corporate not authorized) may indicate the account is being used to initiate unauthorized debits against victim accounts.
falsepositives: Legitimate businesses with high dispute rates due to subscription billing models
Payroll processors during seasonal employment transitions

title: Wire to FATF High-Risk Jurisdiction
description: Detects wire transfers to jurisdictions on the FATF high-risk or increased monitoring lists. While not inherently fraudulent, wires to these jurisdictions combined with other risk factors (new beneficiary, unusual amount, after-hours) significantly elevate the risk of money laundering or fraud monetization.
falsepositives: NGOs and charitable organizations with legitimate operations in high-risk countries
International companies with established supply chains in monitored jurisdictions

title: Payment Instruction Velocity Spike
description: Detects when multiple payment instructions (wires, ACH batches, or internal transfers) are submitted in rapid succession from a single account or user session. High-velocity payment submissions suggest automated or scripted fraud execution, often seen after credential compromise.
falsepositives: Corporate treasury operations submitting batch payments during end-of-day processing
Payroll administrators processing multi-entity payroll batches

title: Mule Rapid ATM Withdrawal After Inbound Transfer
description: Detects cash withdrawals at ATMs occurring shortly after an inbound wire or ACH transfer. Money mules frequently convert electronically received fraud proceeds to cash as quickly as possible to prevent recovery, often hitting daily ATM limits across multiple machines.
falsepositives: Small business owners depositing and immediately withdrawing cash for operational expenses
Individuals receiving legitimate payroll via direct deposit and withdrawing cash

title: Account Age vs Transaction Volume Mismatch
description: Detects accounts less than 90 days old that exhibit transaction volumes exceeding the typical profile for mature accounts. Newly opened accounts with abnormally high volume are a primary indicator of purpose-built mule accounts created specifically to funnel illicit funds.

detection.condition: selection and selection_high_volume | count() by account_id > 20

falsepositives: Legitimate new business accounts with immediate high transaction needs
Student accounts receiving financial aid disbursements at semester start

title: Multi-Bank Funnel Pattern
description: Detects accounts receiving funds from multiple external financial institutions that are then consolidated and sent outbound to a single destination. This funnel pattern is a hallmark of money mule operations where proceeds from multiple fraud victims are aggregated before being laundered.

detection.condition: selection_inbound | count(distinct originating_bank_id) by account_id > 3 and selection_outbound | count(distinct beneficiary_id) by account_id <= 2

falsepositives: Freelancers or consultants receiving payments from multiple clients via different banks
Small businesses with receivables from diverse customer base

title: Crypto Off-Ramp After Wire or ACH Receipt
description: Detects a pattern where an account receives a wire or ACH credit and then promptly initiates a transfer to a known cryptocurrency exchange or digital asset platform. Converting fraud proceeds to cryptocurrency provides near-irreversible laundering, making this a critical monetization indicator.
falsepositives: Legitimate cryptocurrency investors or traders funding exchange accounts from bank proceeds
Businesses with crypto treasury strategies converting fiat after receivables

title: Peer-to-Peer Transfer Chain (Smurfing Pattern)
description: Detects chains of peer-to-peer transfers across multiple accounts where funds move through a sequence of intermediary accounts (A to B to C to D). This smurfing pattern is used to layer fraud proceeds through multiple hops, making tracing difficult.

detection.condition: selection_p2p | count() by account_id > 3 and selection_chain | count(distinct counterparty_account_id) by account_id > 2

falsepositives: Group event organizers collecting and redistributing shared expenses
Family members transferring funds between accounts for household management

title: Mule Recruitment Test Deposit Pattern
description: Detects accounts receiving multiple small "test" deposits from many distinct external sources. Mule recruiters validate new mule accounts by sending micro-deposits from various fraud proceeds before routing larger amounts. The pattern of many small inbound transfers from unrelated senders is highly anomalous for personal accounts.
falsepositives: Account verification micro-deposits from legitimate fintech platforms linking accounts
Social media influencers receiving many small tips or donations

title: Rapid Fund Layering Through Shell Accounts
description: Detects rapid fund movement through multiple accounts with minimal retention time, indicative of layering through shell or pass-through accounts. Funds transit through each account within hours with near-zero balance retention, suggesting the accounts exist solely to obscure the money trail.

detection.condition: selection_pass_through | near selection_rapid_egress by account_id and selection_low_retention | count() by account_id > 3 within 30d

falsepositives: Escrow or settlement accounts that legitimately have rapid pass-through flows
Operating accounts of payment processors or money service businesses

title: Carrier Change Authentication Correlation
description: Detects a carrier or SIM change event immediately followed by an authentication attempt on a banking platform. SIM swap attacks involve social engineering or insider compromise at a mobile carrier to port the victim's phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM, after which the attacker uses SMS-based MFA to access accounts. The tight temporal correlation between carrier change and login is the key indicator.

detection.condition: selection_carrier_change | followed_by selection_auth on phone_number within 120m

falsepositives: Legitimate users who switch carriers and immediately log in to their banking apps
Planned device upgrades where users authenticate on new hardware right after activation

title: New Device High-Value Transaction
description: Detects a high-value financial transaction initiated from a new or previously unknown device shortly after initial authentication. Attackers who have compromised credentials and bypassed MFA via SIM swap typically move quickly to execute high-value transfers from a device with no prior history on the account, exploiting the narrow window before the victim notices.
falsepositives: Customers logging in from a newly purchased device to make a planned large payment
Joint account holders using a device not previously associated with the account

title: MFA Push Bombing
description: Detects rapid repeated MFA push notifications sent to the same user, a technique known as MFA fatigue or push bombing. Attackers who have obtained valid credentials bombard the victim with push authentication requests, hoping the user will approve one out of frustration or confusion, thereby granting the attacker access.

detection.condition: selection | count() by user_id > 5 and count(selection_denied) by user_id > 3

falsepositives: Connectivity issues causing MFA push retries from legitimate authentication flows
Users who accidentally trigger multiple login attempts from different app instances

title: SIM Swap Indicator Chain
description: Detects the full SIM swap attack chain: phone number change followed by password reset followed by high-value account action in rapid sequence. This multi-stage correlation captures the complete attack lifecycle where the attacker first takes over the phone number, then uses it to reset the account password via SMS OTP, and finally executes a high-value transfer or account modification.

detection.condition: stage1_sim_change | followed_by stage2_password_reset | followed_by stage3_high_value_action on user_id within 24h

falsepositives: Legitimate users who change carriers, reset a forgotten password, and then make a large purchase in the same day

title: VoIP Number MFA Enrollment
description: Detects MFA enrollment using VoIP or virtual phone numbers instead of legitimate mobile carrier numbers. Attackers who have compromised an account often enroll a disposable VoIP number (Google Voice, TextNow, Twilio) as the MFA phone to maintain persistent access and intercept future OTP codes without relying on SIM swap persistence.
falsepositives: Legitimate users who use VoIP as their primary phone service
Business accounts that use virtual phone systems for operations

title: MFA Method Downgrade
description: Detects when an account's MFA method is changed from a strong phishing-resistant factor (FIDO2/WebAuthn, hardware token, authenticator app) to a weaker method (SMS OTP, voice call). Attackers who compromise account credentials may downgrade the MFA method to one they can intercept via SIM swap or SS7 exploitation, enabling persistent account takeover.
falsepositives: Users who lose their hardware security key or authenticator app and fall back to SMS temporarily
Account recovery workflows that require temporary MFA method changes

title: Voice Biometric Confidence Score Anomaly for Known Caller
description: Detects when a voice biometric verification score for a previously enrolled caller falls below an acceptable confidence threshold, which may indicate a deepfake or voice-clone attempt impersonating a legitimate customer. Legitimate callers typically produce scores above 85; scores between 40-70 with a previously stable voiceprint warrant investigation.
falsepositives: Caller with a cold, sore throat, or other temporary vocal condition
Poor telephone line quality or high background noise environment
Caller using a different handset or headset than during enrollment

title: Callback Number Mismatch for Claimed Institution
description: Detects when an inbound caller claims to represent a specific financial institution or internal department, but the originating ANI or callback number does not match the institution's known directory of outbound numbers. This is a common indicator of vishing and social engineering, especially when combined with voice-clone technology to impersonate bank officials.
falsepositives: Legitimate bank employee calling from a personal device during off-hours
Third-party call center using non-registered outbound numbers
Recent phone system migration with directory not yet updated

title: Audio Compression Artifacts Indicative of AI-Generated Speech
description: Detects audio streams exhibiting compression artifacts, spectral anomalies, or frequency-band irregularities characteristic of AI-generated or text-to-speech synthesis engines. These include unnaturally uniform pitch contours, missing micro-pauses, absence of breath sounds, and codec artifacts from re-encoding through real-time deepfake pipelines.
falsepositives: Callers using low-bandwidth VoIP connections with heavy compression
Speech impairment conditions producing monotone or atypical vocal patterns
Hearing-impaired callers using text-to-speech relay services legitimately

title: Deepfake Anomalies in Video KYC Session
description: Detects anomalies during video KYC (Know Your Customer) sessions that may indicate the use of deepfake technology. Indicators include irregular frame rates suggesting real-time face-swapping, inconsistent lighting between face and background, lip-sync desynchronization, unnatural eye-blink patterns, and face-boundary artifacts.

detection.condition: selection and (filter_frame_anomaly or filter_lipsync or filter_blink or filter_lighting)

falsepositives: Poor internet connection causing frame drops and variable frame rates
Unusual ambient lighting conditions in the caller's environment
Customer wearing heavy makeup or glasses affecting facial analysis

title: AI-Generated Document Detection in Verification
description: Detects indicators of AI-generated or synthetically created identity documents submitted during verification workflows. Flags include metadata anomalies (missing EXIF data, uniform noise patterns), font rendering inconsistencies, micro-printing irregularities, and GAN-generated portrait artifacts such as asymmetric earrings or irregular hair boundaries.

detection.condition: selection and (filter_metadata or filter_visual or filter_font)

falsepositives: Heavily compressed or photocopied documents with degraded visual quality
Older documents scanned with consumer-grade scanners losing metadata
Legitimately renewed documents with updated security features not yet in template database

title: Real-Time Payment to New Payee After Credential or Contact Change
description: Detects when a real-time or instant payment (Zelle, FedNow, RTP) is initiated to a previously unseen payee within 24 hours of a credential change (password reset, MFA re-enrollment) or contact information update (email, phone, address). This pattern is strongly associated with account takeover followed by immediate monetization via authorized push payment.
falsepositives: Customer who legitimately updated their phone number and then paid a new contractor
Periodic password rotation coinciding with routine bill payment to a new provider

title: Instant Payment Velocity Spike Above 30-Day Baseline
description: Detects a sudden spike in instant payment frequency that significantly exceeds the account's established 30-day baseline. A spike is defined as the current day's instant payment count exceeding 3 standard deviations above the rolling 30-day mean, indicating potential account compromise or mule activity where the account is being drained rapidly.

detection.condition: selection | count() by account_id | compare(op=gt, period=30d, stdev=3)

falsepositives: Small business owner processing seasonal surge in vendor payments
Customer making multiple legitimate payments on a move-in day (deposits, utilities, services)

title: Cross-Platform Deposit and Withdrawal Chain
description: Detects a pattern where funds are received via one payment rail (e.g., ACH, wire) and then immediately sent out via a different payment rail (e.g., Zelle, FedNow) within a short window. This cross-rail chaining is a common layering technique used to obscure the origin of funds and complicate tracing, often associated with money mule operations and authorized push payment fraud monetization.

detection.condition: (selection_inbound and selection_outbound and filter_amount) | temporal(ordered=true, maxspan=4h, by=account_id)

falsepositives: Freelancer receiving ACH payroll and immediately paying rent via Zelle
Business account receiving wire payment and disbursing to vendors via instant payment

title: Repeated A2A Payments at Maximum Per-Transaction Limit
description: Detects multiple account-to-account payments where each transaction is at or near the maximum per-transaction limit (e.g., $2,500 for Zelle, $500,000 for FedNow). Fraudsters often structure payments at the exact limit to maximize extraction speed while avoiding aggregate-amount alerts, a behavior rarely seen in legitimate consumer transactions.

detection.condition: selection and filter_at_limit | count() by account_id > 3

falsepositives: Customer making a large one-time purchase split across multiple payments at platform limits
Business account regularly transacting at high values for legitimate operations

title: New Account Sending Multiple Instant Payments
description: Detects accounts less than 30 days old that initiate multiple instant payments within a short time window. Newly opened accounts used for rapid instant-payment disbursement are a strong indicator of synthetic identity fraud or mule accounts created specifically for the monetization phase of a fraud scheme.

detection.condition: selection and filter_new_account | count() by account_id > 5

falsepositives: Newly opened business account setting up recurring vendor payments
College student opening account and paying multiple roommates for shared expenses

title: Zelle Recipient Enumeration via Multiple Failed Lookups
description: Detects multiple failed Zelle recipient lookups from a single account or session, which may indicate enumeration activity. Attackers probe email addresses and phone numbers to identify which are registered with Zelle before launching targeted social engineering or authorized push payment attacks against confirmed users.
falsepositives: User trying to send money to friends who have not yet enrolled in Zelle
Administrative staff searching for payees across a new vendor list

title: Real-Time Payment Followed by Immediate Refund or Return Request
description: Detects a pattern where a real-time payment (RTP or FedNow) is sent and then an immediate refund, return, or Request for Return of Funds (RROF) is submitted within a short window. This pattern may indicate a double-dip fraud scheme where the sender initiates an irrevocable payment, then exploits the refund process to recover funds while the recipient also retains them.
falsepositives: Legitimate duplicate payment correction where customer realizes the error immediately
Merchant-initiated refund for cancelled service following immediate payment

title: Fake Tracking ID (FTID) Refund Fraud Indicators
description: Detects indicators of fake tracking ID (FTID) refund fraud, where a customer claims a package was not received or returned by providing a manipulated or fabricated tracking number. Indicators include tracking numbers that show delivery to the carrier facility but not to the customer address, tracking IDs associated with lightweight packages inconsistent with the order, or reuse of known FTID patterns across multiple refund claims.

detection.condition: selection and (filter_tracking_anomaly or filter_weight or filter_known_pattern)

falsepositives: Carrier mis-scan delivering to wrong address requiring legitimate reshipment
Lightweight promotional items or gift cards with valid low-weight tracking

title: Abnormally High Refund Rate Per Customer Account
description: Detects customer accounts with an abnormally high refund-to-order ratio over a rolling window. Accounts exceeding a refund rate of 40% across 10 or more orders within 90 days are flagged as potential refund abusers or participants in refunding-as-a-service (RaaS) schemes, where professional refunders exploit return policies systematically.

aggregation.condition:
selection
| groupby(customer_account_id)
| where count(event_type='refund_issued') / count(event_type='order_completed') > 0.4
| where count(event_type='order_completed') >= 10

falsepositives: Customers with legitimate sizing issues making frequent clothing returns
Product quality issues causing high return rates for specific SKUs across multiple customers

title: Triangulation Fraud Shipping Pattern Detection
description: Detects orders where the shipping address differs from the billing address and matches known drop-ship or reshipping patterns associated with triangulation fraud. In triangulation fraud, a fraudster lists goods on a marketplace, collects payment from a victim buyer, then purchases the item from a legitimate retailer using stolen payment credentials, shipping directly to the victim. Indicators include shipping to known drop addresses, freight forwarders, or addresses seen across multiple unrelated accounts.

detection.condition: selection and (filter_drop_address or filter_shared_address or filter_velocity)

falsepositives: Legitimate gift orders shipped to recipients at different addresses
Corporate purchasing departments using centralized receiving addresses
Customers shipping to workplace address for package security

title: Return Without Receipt Clustering by Customer or Region
description: Detects clusters of product returns submitted without receipts or order references from the same customer identity or geographic region. Organized return fraud rings often exploit no-receipt return policies by using stolen merchandise or purchasing items specifically for return, concentrating activity across nearby store locations or using multiple accounts linked to the same region.
falsepositives: Customers who frequently lose receipts for legitimate purchases
Holiday season returns where gift recipients do not have original receipts

title: High-Value Item Not Received Claims Exceeding Threshold
description: Detects "item not received" (INR) claims filed on high-value orders that exceed a configurable dollar threshold. High-value INR claims are a primary vector for refund fraud, particularly when the delivery confirmation shows successful delivery. Repeated INR claims on expensive items from the same account or device fingerprint are strong indicators of first-party fraud or professional refunding services.

detection.condition: selection and filter_high_value and (filter_delivery_confirmed or filter_repeat)

falsepositives: Legitimate porch piracy where delivered package was stolen from doorstep
Carrier misdelivery to wrong address with GPS confirmation error

title: Excessive Promotional Code or Coupon Abuse from Related Accounts
description: Detects excessive use of promotional codes, referral bonuses, or coupon offers from accounts that share common attributes such as device fingerprint, IP address, payment method, or shipping address. This pattern indicates promo abuse rings that create multiple accounts to exploit new-customer or referral promotions repeatedly, often using synthetic or stolen identities.

detection.condition: selection and (filter_device_cluster or filter_ip_cluster or filter_payment_cluster or filter_new_account)

falsepositives: Family members on shared household network legitimately using individual promotions
Corporate office where multiple employees order from same IP using valid individual accounts

title: DPRK IT Worker Resume Geographic Mismatch
description: Detects job applicants whose resume combines a U.S. residential address with education credentials from non-North American institutions (Singapore, Japan, Hong Kong, China, South Korea). This pattern is a key DPRK IT worker indicator documented by FBI IC3 and DOJ enforcement actions. Legitimate applicants with this profile exist, but the combination with thin credit files or recently created LinkedIn profiles significantly elevates risk.
falsepositives: Legitimate international students who studied abroad and relocated to the U.S.
H-1B visa holders with non-North American education backgrounds
Recent immigrants with legitimately thin credit histories

title: VPN/Proxy Login Anomaly — Astrill or Residential Proxy
description: Detects corporate VPN authentication events originating from known Astrill VPN infrastructure, residential proxy services, or connection patterns indicating VPN-over-VPN layering. DPRK IT workers route connections through Astrill VPN to U.S.-based proxy laptops before connecting to corporate infrastructure, creating a characteristic multi-hop pattern with elevated latency and IP reputation indicators.

detection.condition: selection and (filter_astrill or filter_residential_proxy or filter_vpn_layering)

falsepositives: Employees in countries where VPN use is required for internet access
Employees using personal VPN services for privacy while on public networks

title: Multi-Operator Behavioral Shift — Timezone and Communication Anomaly
description: Detects behavioral patterns suggesting multiple operators are sharing a single employee identity. Indicators include login activity spanning incompatible timezones within a single day, significant shifts in communication style or vocabulary between time windows, and device fingerprint changes that correlate with timezone transitions. DPRK IT workers often operate in shifts from different locations using the same stolen identity.
falsepositives: Employees who travel frequently across timezone boundaries
Employees using multiple devices across home and office locations

title: Bulk Code Repository Clone by New Employee
description: Detects a new employee (within first 14 days of onboarding) cloning or downloading multiple code repositories, especially repositories outside their assigned team or project scope. DPRK IT workers frequently begin exfiltrating source code within hours of gaining access, cloning entire organizational repositories to personal GitHub accounts or external cloud storage.
falsepositives: New employees in platform engineering or DevOps roles who legitimately need broad repository access
Engineers onboarding onto large monorepo projects that require full clone

title: Credential Store Access Anomaly During Onboarding
description: Detects new employees accessing browser credential stores, password managers, API key management systems, or SSO session token stores at rates significantly above peer baselines during the first 14 days of employment. DPRK IT workers harvest credentials, session cookies, and API keys early in their tenure for exfiltration to DPRK cyber units and as leverage for post-termination extortion.
falsepositives: Developers configuring CI/CD pipelines that require multiple API keys during initial setup
Security engineers performing credential audits as part of onboarding tasks

title: Salary Direct Deposit Rapid Cryptocurrency Conversion
description: Detects patterns where salary direct deposit payments are rapidly converted to cryptocurrency (USDT, USDC, BTC) within 48 hours of deposit, particularly when the receiving account was recently opened or when multiple employee accounts show the same conversion pattern through the same exchange or payment processor. DPRK IT workers convert salary to cryptocurrency for transfer to regime-controlled wallets, often using daily conversion limits to avoid AML alerts.
falsepositives: Employees who routinely invest a portion of salary in cryptocurrency through automated transfers
Cryptocurrency industry employees whose compensation is partially crypto-denominated

title: Post-Termination Data Extortion Indicator
description: Detects indicators of post-termination data extortion, where a recently terminated or resigned employee communicates ransom demands referencing specific internal proprietary code, documents, or trade secrets. DPRK IT workers have escalated to this tactic since mid-2024, threatening to publish exfiltrated source code on public repositories or sell proprietary data unless payment is made. Indicators include communication from personal channels containing references to internal systems, and the appearance of company code on public GitHub repositories created by former employee-linked accounts.
falsepositives: Whistleblower disclosures through proper legal channels
Former employee academic publications referencing general (non-proprietary) work

title: E-Skimmer Script Injection on Payment Pages
description: Detects unauthorized JavaScript injection on e-commerce payment pages by identifying Content Security Policy violations, unexpected external script loads from newly registered domains, and unauthorized Google Tag Manager container modifications. Magecart-style e-skimmer operators inject malicious scripts through CMS exploitation, compromised third-party libraries, or GTM container abuse. The "Sniffer by Fleras" MaaS platform accounts for 26% of all infections, and GTM container abuse has become a primary delivery vector due to GTM's trusted status in most CSP configurations. PCI DSS 4.0 Requirement 6.4.3 mandates automated script integrity monitoring on payment pages, making this detection a compliance requirement as well as a security control.

detection.condition: selection_csp or (selection_script_load and not filter_authorized_scripts) or selection_gtm_modification

falsepositives: Legitimate third-party marketing or analytics script deployments not yet added to the CSP whitelist
Authorized GTM container updates that were not pre-registered in the change management system
A/B testing platforms injecting scripts on checkout pages as part of authorized experiments

title: Blockchain C2 and WebSocket Exfiltration from Payment Pages
description: Detects payment page scripts making calls to blockchain RPC endpoints or establishing WebSocket connections to unknown servers, indicating potential e-skimmer data exfiltration via blockchain-based command-and-control infrastructure. Advanced Magecart variants observed in 2025 use a loader script on the compromised site that queries a blockchain smart contract (Ethereum, BNB Chain) to retrieve the address of a second-stage payload server, then establishes a WebSocket connection for both payload delivery and data exfiltration. This technique provides censorship-resistant C2 that cannot be disrupted through conventional domain seizure or hosting provider takedown. Detection focuses on identifying JSON-RPC calls to blockchain node endpoints (Infura, Alchemy, direct nodes) and WebSocket connections to non-payment-related servers originating from payment page context.
falsepositives: Web3-native e-commerce platforms that legitimately interact with blockchain for payment processing (e.g., cryptocurrency payment acceptance)
Customer support chat widgets using WebSocket connections on checkout pages
Real-time inventory or pricing update feeds using WebSocket on payment pages

title: Unauthorized Checkout Page DOM Modification
description: Detects modifications to checkout page DOM elements — including payment form fields, submit buttons, and iframe injections — that occur outside authorized deployment windows or without corresponding change management records. E-skimmer operators manipulate checkout page DOM to inject fake payment form overlays, intercept form submission events, or create invisible iframes that mirror payment forms to capture card data. Legitimate checkout page modifications should only occur during scheduled deployment windows and should be tracked in version control and change management systems. Any DOM mutation on payment form elements that does not correlate with an authorized release is a high-confidence indicator of e-skimmer injection. This rule supports PCI DSS 4.0 Requirement 6.4.3 for script and content integrity monitoring on payment pages.

detection.condition: selection and not filter_authorized_deployment and not filter_framework_mutations

falsepositives: Legitimate hotfix deployments that bypass standard change management windows
Browser extensions that modify page DOM for accessibility purposes
Payment processor SDK updates that modify form elements dynamically

title: Scam Merchant High-Velocity Transaction Pattern
description: Detects merchant accounts exhibiting high initial transaction velocity, elevated chargeback ratios, and short account age — a pattern consistent with purchase scam merchant operations. Recorded Future identified 3,600+ scam merchant accounts in 2025, a 2.5x increase from 2024, operating across 40+ countries and 230+ acquirers. Scam merchants typically process high transaction volumes within their first 30-90 days to extract maximum revenue before chargeback volume triggers acquirer intervention and account termination. Normal new merchant ramp-up is fewer than 50 transactions per day in the first 30 days, ramping to 200+ by day 90. Scam merchants frequently exceed 200 transactions per day within the first two weeks, combined with chargeback rates exceeding 1.5% within 60 days of account opening. This rule also flags merchants with account ages under 90 days that have already accumulated chargeback ratios above scheme monitoring thresholds.
falsepositives: Legitimate new merchants running launch promotions or flash sales with high initial transaction volumes
Seasonal merchants (holiday, event-driven) with compressed selling periods
Marketplace merchants migrating transaction history from another acquirer

title: Subscription Trap Billing Pattern Detection
description: Detects recurring billing patterns characteristic of subscription trap scam merchants, where initial low-value trial charges are followed by significantly higher recurring charges to merchants with elevated dispute rates. Purchase scam operators enroll victims in subscription billing through obscured terms buried in checkout flows — initial charges are typically under $10 (trial pricing) while subsequent recurring charges escalate to $50-$200+ per cycle. Recorded Future identified this pattern across scam merchant networks in 2025, with some operations adding a secondary "transaction recovery service" charge in H2 2025. Detection focuses on merchants where the ratio of maximum to minimum charge amount exceeds 5:1, recurring billing constitutes more than 30% of transactions, initial charges are below $10, and the merchant has an elevated dispute rate relative to its age and category. Normal subscription merchants show a recurring billing enrollment rate of 5-15% of total transactions, and legitimate trial-to-paid conversions typically maintain a ratio under 3:1.

detection.condition: selection and filter_amount_disparity and filter_recurring_ratio and filter_dispute_rate

falsepositives: Legitimate subscription businesses with low introductory pricing and standard price escalation (e.g., streaming services, SaaS trial-to-paid conversion)
Freemium services with significant price differences between free trial and premium tiers
Utility or insurance merchants with variable billing amounts that fluctuate based on usage

title: Wallet Provisioning Following OTP Interception Indicator
description: Detects digital wallet provisioning events where the OTP or verification code was delivered within minutes of a social engineering indicator, such as an inbound call from a suspicious source, a phishing link click, or a smishing response. Legitimate wallet provisioning is typically self-initiated, with OTP-to-provisioning intervals of 30-120 seconds. When provisioning occurs within 15 seconds of OTP delivery, or when OTP delivery is preceded by a phishing or social engineering indicator within a 30-minute window, this strongly suggests automated interception-to-provision attack chains associated with digital wallet fraud (TP-0037). The card provisioning attempt is the critical disruption point where refined controls can prevent downstream contactless fraud.
falsepositives: Legitimate cardholders who provision wallets very quickly after receiving OTP
Tech-savvy users with automated provisioning workflows on trusted devices
Corporate card administrators provisioning multiple devices in rapid succession

title: NFC Relay Geographic Impossibility on Contactless Transaction
description: Detects contactless (tap-to-pay) transactions where the POS terminal location is geographically impossible given the cardholder's last known location. When a contactless transaction occurs at a POS terminal more than 100 kilometers from the cardholder's most recent authenticated activity (mobile banking login, ATM withdrawal, or prior in-person transaction) within a timeframe that makes physical travel impossible, it indicates NFC relay (ghost-tapping) or unauthorized wallet token use. This rule specifically targets the Phase 4 execution stage of digital wallet fraud and NFC relay attacks (TP-0037), where money mules conduct contactless purchases using relayed card data at POS terminals geographically distant from the legitimate cardholder.

detection.condition: selection and correlation_geographic and filter_distance and filter_travel_impossible

falsepositives: Cardholders who travel by air and conduct transactions shortly after landing
Corporate cards used by multiple authorized individuals in different locations
Mobile banking geolocation errors due to VPN or proxy usage

title: Ghost-Tap Multi-Terminal Contactless Velocity Anomaly
description: Detects multiple contactless transactions from the same wallet token or card credential across multiple distinct POS terminals within a short timeframe. Normal cardholder behavior produces a maximum of 2-3 contactless transactions per hour across different terminals during shopping activity. NFC relay (ghost-tapping) operations using tools such as SuperCardX, NFCGate, Hyper NFC, or Valkirie NFC enable simultaneous contactless transactions at multiple POS terminals by relaying stolen card data to multiple money mule devices. This rule detects the Phase 4 execution pattern of TP-0037 where the same wallet token appears at 3 or more distinct POS terminals within 30 minutes, a pattern that is physically impossible for a single cardholder and pathognomonic for NFC relay fraud.

detection.condition: selection and aggregation and (filter_multi_terminal or filter_multi_location)

falsepositives: Family members sharing a card account who shop at different stores simultaneously (rare with tokenized wallets as each device has a unique token)
POS terminal ID reassignment or misconfiguration causing apparent multi-terminal usage

title: Card Testing Micro-Authorization Velocity Spike
description: Detects high velocity of sub-dollar ($0.01-$0.99) authorization attempts from the same merchant or source against multiple distinct card numbers, a pattern characteristic of automated card testing operations. Recorded Future's 2025 report identified over 1,350 tester merchant accounts, with 94% being newly registered merchants. Normal merchant sub-dollar authorization rates are under 0.5% of total authorizations. Card testing operations generate authorization streams where sub-dollar transactions dominate, decline rates exceed 70%, and unique card numbers per source per hour reach 50-500+. This rule targets Phase 4 of TP-0038, detecting the execution of automated card validation at scale through micro-authorization patterns that deviate from legitimate merchant transaction profiles.

detection.condition: selection and aggregation and filter_card_diversity and filter_decline_rate

falsepositives: Subscription services performing periodic micro-authorizations for card-on-file validation
Payment processors conducting legitimate batch card verification for account updates
Charitable organizations processing high volumes of small donations during fundraising events

title: BIN Enumeration Sequential Card Number Attack
description: Detects sequential or near-sequential card number authorization attempts sharing the same Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefix with incremental variation in the remaining digits. BIN enumeration attacks generate valid card numbers by iterating through possible combinations within a BIN range, validating each against live payment infrastructure through sub-dollar authorization requests. Sequential card numbers from the same BIN prefix have a zero false positive rate for legitimate merchants — this pattern is exclusively associated with fraudulent enumeration. Recorded Future's 2025 report documents BIN attacks as a primary method for generating valid card credentials for downstream fraud, with enumerated cards feeding into card testing (TP-0038), digital wallet provisioning (TP-0037), and card-not-present fraud operations. This rule targets Phase 4 of TP-0038.

detection.condition: selection and aggregation_bin and filter_sequential and filter_decline

falsepositives: Corporate card programs where cards are issued with sequential numbers to the same organization (extremely rare in authorization streams)

title: Agent Intent Manipulation — Purchase Divergence from User Intent
description: Detects transactions initiated by AI agents where the product or service purchased diverges significantly from the user's stated intent or historical purchasing patterns, or where the receiving merchant is flagged as high-risk. This rule targets Phase 3 (Positioning) of agentic commerce fraud, where threat actors manipulate agent purchasing intent to redirect transactions to attacker-controlled merchants or execute purchases that do not reflect the consumer's actual desires. Key indicators include purchases in product categories the user has never engaged with, transactions at merchants created within the last 30 days, transaction amounts exceeding 3x the user's historical average, and merchants with elevated risk scores.
falsepositives: Users exploring new product categories via agent for the first time
Legitimate purchases from newly launched merchants or startups
Gift purchases in categories outside user's typical patterns
Agent executing user-directed purchases at premium pricing (luxury goods)

title: Agent Transaction Velocity Anomaly
description: Detects AI agent-initiated transactions at velocities exceeding human purchasing patterns, including multiple purchases per minute and simultaneous multi-merchant purchases within a single agent session. This rule targets Phase 4 (Execution) of agentic commerce fraud, where compromised or manipulated agents execute unauthorized transactions at machine speed. Normal agent purchasing velocity is 1-5 purchases per user session with 2-15 minutes of comparison shopping per purchase. Velocities exceeding 10x human baseline (more than 5 transactions per minute or purchases across more than 3 merchants within a 60-second window) suggest automated fraud exploitation rather than legitimate agent-assisted shopping.
falsepositives: Agent bulk-purchasing identical items across merchants for price comparison fulfillment
Corporate procurement agents executing pre-approved batch purchase orders
Agent re-executing failed transactions in rapid succession due to payment gateway timeouts

title: BNPL Account Opening Risk Signal Cluster
description: Detects BNPL account applications exhibiting multiple risk signals indicative of synthetic identity fraud. Specifically targets accounts opened with email domains less than 30 days old, minimal digital footprint (score below 0.2), and patterns consistent with emulator-based mass account creation. BNPL providers using soft-check-only approval processes are particularly vulnerable to synthetic identities that pass initial verification but exhibit these digital footprint anomalies. This rule supports detection at Phase 2 of TP-0040 by identifying high-risk onboarding patterns before the synthetic identity progresses to credit grooming and multi-provider stacking.
falsepositives: Young consumers opening their first financial accounts with limited digital history
New email service adopters who recently migrated to a new email provider
Immigrants or expats establishing new digital identities in a new country

title: BNPL Multi-Provider Application Velocity
description: Detects identities applying to three or more distinct BNPL providers within a 72-hour window, a pattern characteristic of multi-provider stacking operations. Legitimate consumers rarely apply to more than two BNPL providers within a week. Synthetic identity rings exploit the absence of cross-bureau BNPL loan reporting to accumulate $3,000-$15,000 in aggregate exposure across providers while each provider sees only their individual exposure. This rule requires consortium-level data sharing to be effective, as individual providers cannot detect cross-provider application velocity in isolation. At Phase 3 of TP-0040, multi-provider stacking represents the critical positioning step before coordinated bust-out execution.
falsepositives: Consumers comparison shopping across BNPL providers for a single large purchase
Corporate purchasing agents setting up multiple BNPL relationships for business procurement

title: BNPL Spending Step-Up to Limit Bust-Out Pattern
description: Detects the characteristic spending escalation pattern of BNPL bust-out fraud, where accounts begin with small purchases (under $50) during a credit grooming phase, then rapidly escalate to purchases consuming 85% or more of the available credit limit within 14 days. This pattern distinguishes synthetic bust-out operations from legitimate consumer behavior, where spending typically ramps gradually over weeks to months. Recorded in organized rings deploying 50-1,000+ synthetic identities, the grooming-to-bustout transition represents the highest-confidence detection window for TP-0040 Phase 4 execution, as the sharp behavioral shift from conservative to aggressive spending is difficult for fraudsters to avoid without sacrificing the speed required for coordinated multi-provider bust-out.

detection.condition: selection and filter_first_order and filter_limit_usage and filter_timespan

falsepositives: Legitimate consumers building confidence with a new BNPL provider before making a planned large purchase
Seasonal shopping patterns where consumers save large purchases for sales events

title: BNPL Item-Not-Received Claim Velocity
description: Detects accounts filing three or more item-not-received (INR) claims within a 90-day rolling window where the average disputed order value exceeds $300. Legitimate INR dispute rates are under 1% of orders, with most disputes involving genuine delivery failures. Organized phantom delivery fraud and friendly fraud operations systematically file INR claims after receiving goods, targeting high-value orders to maximize returns. This rule supports TP-0040 Phase 4 detection by identifying accounts exhibiting claim patterns consistent with organized INR abuse rather than genuine delivery issues. The $300 average threshold filters out low-value legitimate disputes while capturing the high-value targeting characteristic of organized fraud.
falsepositives: Legitimate delivery failures in areas with known courier reliability issues
Bulk purchasers with higher absolute dispute counts due to high order volumes
Seasonal delivery disruptions during peak shipping periods

title: BNPL Cross-Account Device Clustering
description: Detects four or more distinct BNPL accounts created from or accessed by the same device fingerprint within a 30-day window, indicating potential synthetic identity ring activity or account farming operations. Normal BNPL usage involves 1-2 accounts per device over 12 months. Emulator-based mass account opening tools with device fingerprint spoofing can create dozens of accounts per day from a single physical device, but sophisticated device fingerprinting systems can detect emulator signatures and fingerprint collision patterns. This rule supports TP-0040 Phase 3 detection by identifying device-level clustering that precedes multi-provider stacking and coordinated bust-out.
falsepositives: Shared household devices used by multiple family members for individual BNPL accounts
Retail kiosk or shared terminal devices in store environments
Workplace devices used by employees for personal BNPL accounts

title: RDGA Registration Timing Pattern Detection
description: Detects clusters of domain registrations exhibiting algorithmically regular timing intervals in zone file diffs, a hallmark of Registered Domain Generation Algorithm (RDGA) infrastructure provisioning. Legitimate bulk registrations by brand protection services or hosting providers typically show irregular, human-driven timing patterns. RDGA tooling operates programmatically, producing registration bursts with low standard deviation in inter-registration intervals. This rule alerts when a cluster of newly registered domains exceeds a size threshold and the inter-registration timing standard deviation falls below a regularity threshold, indicating automated generation. Supports TP-0041 Phase 2 detection of RDGA-based initial access infrastructure staging.
falsepositives: Brand protection services registering defensive domains in automated batches
Large hosting providers onboarding customer domains via API
Domain portfolio companies performing scheduled bulk acquisitions

title: RDGA Nameserver Clustering Anomaly
description: Detects disproportionate concentration of newly registered domains pointing to the same nameserver infrastructure within a 24-hour window. RDGA operators typically provision hundreds or thousands of domains but anchor them to a small set of nameservers they control, creating a fan-in pattern that is statistically anomalous compared to legitimate registrar or hosting provider distributions. Legitimate nameservers serving large numbers of new domains tend to be well-known hosting or registrar nameservers with established reputation. This rule identifies nameserver endpoints receiving an abnormal influx of newly registered domain delegations, filtering out known hosting infrastructure. Supports TP-0041 Phase 2 detection of RDGA nameserver infrastructure consolidation.

detection.condition: selection and aggregation and not exclusion

falsepositives: New hosting providers onboarding large customer bases rapidly
DNS migration events where many domains switch nameservers simultaneously
Reseller registrars consolidating domains under shared nameserver infrastructure

title: RDGA Registrar Concentration Anomaly
description: Detects anomalous concentration of new domain registrations at a single registrar that share lexical similarity patterns and nameserver infrastructure, indicating RDGA-driven bulk registration campaigns. Threat actors frequently exploit registrars with weak abuse controls, automated APIs, or low-cost bulk pricing to register large volumes of algorithmically generated domains. This rule correlates three signals: high registration volume at a single registrar, lexical similarity among the registered domain names (e.g., consonant-vowel patterns, character n-gram overlap, or string edit distance clustering), and shared nameserver delegation. The combination of these factors distinguishes RDGA activity from legitimate bulk registration by portfolio investors or brand protection services. Supports TP-0041 Phase 2 detection of registrar abuse for RDGA infrastructure provisioning.

detection.condition: selection and aggregation and lexical_similarity and nameserver_overlap

falsepositives: Domain portfolio investors acquiring thematically similar domain names in bulk
Brand protection services registering typosquatting variants defensively
New gTLD land-rush registrations with common keyword patterns

title: TDS Redirect Chain Depth Anomaly
description: Detects HTTP redirect chains (302, 301, or JavaScript-based redirects) exceeding a depth threshold where intermediate nodes are newly registered domains or have low reputation scores, indicating Traffic Distribution System (TDS) abuse. Legitimate web redirects rarely exceed 3 hops and typically traverse well-known CDN, analytics, or marketing infrastructure. TDS chains commonly use 4-7 or more hops through disposable intermediary domains to obfuscate the final destination, evade URL blocklists, and enable real-time traffic steering. Each hop in a TDS chain may perform user-agent filtering, geolocation checks, or bot detection before forwarding. This rule correlates redirect depth with domain age and reputation of intermediate nodes to distinguish malicious TDS chains from legitimate multi-hop redirects. Supports TP-0042 Phase 3 detection of TDS positioning and traffic funneling infrastructure.
falsepositives: Advertising technology redirect chains through multiple ad exchanges
Affiliate marketing link chains with multiple tracking intermediaries
URL shortener services chained together by users

title: TDS Cloaking Behavior Detection
description: Detects domains serving divergent content based on visitor attributes such as geolocation, device fingerprint, or user agent, a technique known as cloaking. TDS operators serve benign or empty content to security scanner user agents (e.g., Googlebot, bingbot, crawlers), datacenter IP ranges, and known security vendor IP addresses, while delivering redirects or malicious content to residential IP addresses and consumer device fingerprints. This rule identifies cloaking by correlating response divergence across multiple request profiles to the same URL: when a domain returns substantially different HTTP response codes, content lengths, or redirect targets for scanner versus residential visitor profiles within a detection window, it indicates intentional cloaking. Supports TP-0042 Phase 3 detection of TDS cloaking used to evade automated threat scanning and URL reputation systems.

detection.condition: selection and scanner_response and residential_response and content_divergence

falsepositives: Geo-restricted content delivery serving different pages by region legitimately
A/B testing platforms serving variant content to different visitor segments
Bot management solutions intentionally serving CAPTCHAs to automated traffic

title: TDS Shared Infrastructure Correlation
description: Detects domains from different apparent campaigns sharing hosting infrastructure, nameservers, or registration patterns — indicating a common TDS operator serving multiple affiliates. This rule performs graph-based correlation by identifying domains resolving to the same IP CIDR block with different registrant information but similar registration timing. TDS operators frequently reuse backend infrastructure across campaigns while rotating customer-facing domains, creating detectable infrastructure overlap patterns. Shared nameserver configurations, co-located IP assignments within the same /24 CIDR, and registration timestamps clustered within hours are strong indicators of centralized TDS management across ostensibly independent fraud campaigns.
falsepositives: Shared hosting providers where unrelated customers legitimately occupy the same CIDR block
CDN or cloud provider IP ranges that host many unrelated domains
Domain parking services that cluster domains on shared infrastructure

title: AI-Generated Domain Lexical Pattern Detection
description: Detects domain registrations exhibiting lexical patterns consistent with AI-generated names: natural-language-like domain names that are grammatically plausible but not established brands, unusual TLD selection patterns, and registration in bulk with similar lexical characteristics. Large language models can produce domain names that bypass traditional DGA detection because they use real words and plausible constructions rather than random character strings. This rule identifies clusters of newly registered domains sharing lexical similarity scores above threshold, exhibiting natural-language n-gram distributions, and registered through the same registrar within a compressed time window. AI-generated domain portfolios tend to follow detectable stylistic patterns such as consistent word-count, hyphenation style, and semantic category clustering that distinguish them from organic registrations.
falsepositives: Legitimate brand portfolio registrations by marketing agencies
Domain investment companies registering descriptive keyword domains
New product launch campaigns registering multiple related domains

title: Bulk Let's Encrypt Certificate Issuance Clustering
description: Detects clusters of Let's Encrypt certificate issuances for domains sharing nameserver or registrar characteristics within a short time window. RDGA and AI-generated campaigns frequently provision certificates in bulk immediately after registration to enable HTTPS on fraudulent landing pages and phishing sites. Legitimate bulk certificate issuance typically occurs through established organizations with consistent registration history. This rule identifies anomalous spikes in certificate issuance where multiple domains share infrastructure indicators such as common nameservers, registrar, or IP allocation, and certificates are issued within hours of domain registration. The combination of rapid registration-to-certificate timing and shared infrastructure strongly indicates coordinated fraudulent domain provisioning for campaign deployment.
falsepositives: Large-scale legitimate deployments using automated certificate provisioning (e.g., SaaS platforms onboarding customer domains)
Hosting providers that auto-provision Let's Encrypt certificates for new customer sites
CDN providers issuing certificates for newly onboarded domains

title: Zone File Daily Diff Anomaly Detection
description: Detects anomalous patterns in daily zone file diffs: unusual volume of new registrations in a single TLD, concentration of registrations at specific registrars, or patterns suggesting algorithmic generation including lexical similarity, sequential naming, and entropy clustering. Zone file diffs provide a ground-truth view of new domain registrations across gTLDs and many ccTLDs. Fraudulent campaigns using RDGA, TDS, or AI-generated domain strategies produce detectable statistical anomalies in daily diff data — particularly registrar concentration spikes, abnormal per-TLD registration volumes, and clusters of domains with similar character distribution or word structure. This rule establishes rolling baselines for registrar-TLD combinations and alerts when daily new registration counts exceed three standard deviations from the 30-day rolling mean, or when entropy analysis reveals clustering indicative of algorithmic or template-based domain generation.
falsepositives: Promotional pricing events by registrars that cause legitimate registration spikes
New TLD launches or sunrise periods with high legitimate registration volume
Large enterprise domain portfolio acquisitions through a single registrar

title: State-Criminal Shared Infrastructure Overlap
description: Detect when IP addresses, nameservers, or hosting infrastructure previously attributed to state-sponsored threat actors begin hosting domains or services associated with criminal campaigns (or vice versa). Uses graph-based detection to identify shared IP CIDR blocks, nameserver overlap, and temporal proximity of domain registrations. State-criminal convergence represents an emerging threat where nation-state infrastructure is repurposed for financially motivated crime, or criminal bulletproof hosting serves dual-use purposes for both espionage and fraud operations. This detection correlates threat intelligence attribution data with passive DNS records and infrastructure registration metadata to surface shared hosting patterns across historically distinct threat actor categories.
falsepositives: Shared hosting providers with both state-actor and criminal clients
CDN/cloud infrastructure serving diverse customer bases

title: Sanctions Designation Infrastructure Migration
description: Detect infrastructure migration patterns following OFAC sanctions designations. Domains previously resolving to sanctioned entity IP ranges migrate to new hosting within 7-30 days of designation, retaining similar DNS configurations but different IP blocks. Tracks Aeza to Smart Digital/Datavice and Garantex to Grinex migration patterns. Sanctions designations trigger predictable infrastructure migration behavior where sanctioned entities rapidly move domains and services to new IP ranges while preserving nameserver configurations, MX records, and SSL certificate patterns. This detection correlates OFAC designation dates with zone file diffs and passive DNS records to identify domains that migrate from sanctioned IP ranges to new hosting within the expected evasion window, flagging infrastructure that retains structural DNS similarity despite IP block changes.
falsepositives: Legitimate hosting provider changes coinciding with sanctions timelines
CDN failover events

title: Stablecoin Settlement Pattern Anomaly
description: Detect stablecoin transaction patterns consistent with sanctions evasion settlement. Identifies Monday-Friday volume surges with weekend drops (business settlement pattern), transaction clustering to known no-KYC exchange addresses, and volume patterns matching the A7A5 ruble-backed stablecoin profile. Sanctions evasion through stablecoin settlement produces distinctive temporal patterns that mirror traditional business settlement cycles rather than typical retail crypto trading behavior. The weekday-to-weekend volume ratio, combined with clustering of transactions to addresses associated with no-KYC exchanges, provides a high-confidence signal for institutional sanctions evasion activity. This detection establishes rolling baselines for address-level volume patterns and alerts when weekday-weekend ratios and exchange clustering metrics exceed defined thresholds.
falsepositives: Legitimate institutional settlement patterns
OTC desk activity during business hours

title: BPH Rebranding Chain Detection
